title: Guardrails: safe-degrade Optimize apply when eval runner is unavailable (block vs manual approval by tier)
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: - Optimize apply now fails closed when guardrails gating cannot be executed due to eval-runner unavailability, with tier-based behavior (blocked vs manual approval). - New gating failure reason + audit fields to distinguish quality failures from system failures.
commits: control-plane: add eval runner health state + circuit breaker
policy-engine: add SafeDegradePolicy (tier -> action) and decision plumbing
optimize-api: return deterministic response on runner outage + retry hints
audit: emit system_unavailable details for gating failures
tests: add integration coverage for outage/partial outage cases
description:
Context: Optimize apply is gated by guardrails evals. During pilot we saw timeouts/backlog conditions in the async eval runner (staging + one internal canary), which led to ambiguous UX ("timeout") and inconsistent behavior across tiers. This PR implements safe-degrade behavior so that an eval-runner outage/partial outage produces a deterministic gating outcome, with tier-based policy: self-serve/hosted tiers fail closed (apply is blocked), while enterprise tiers can proceed only via a manual approval pathway (existing override mechanism, with additional audit fields) when enabled by rollout flag.

What changed: (1) Control plane now maintains an EvalRunnerHealth state derived from runner heartbeat + queue lag metrics and wraps calls with a small circuit breaker (opens after consecutive failures/timeouts; half-open probes every 30s). (2) Policy engine introduces a SafeDegradePolicy that maps tenant tier to an action when the gating system is unavailable: BLOCK (default) or REQUIRE_MANUAL_APPROVAL (enterprise-only; still requires permissions). (3) Optimize apply handler distinguishes quality failures from system unavailability. When runner health is UNAVAILABLE (or circuit breaker open), apply returns a structured gating response with failure_reason=SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE, retry_after_seconds, and next_step UI hint. (4) Audit logging adds fields to make system failures queryable without inflating cardinality: gating_system_state, circuit_breaker_state, and a normalized unavailable_reason enum.

Tier policy (initial): - Hosted Free/Pro/Team: BLOCK. - Dedicated + Private (Enterprise): REQUIRE_MANUAL_APPROVAL (behind flag optimize.guardrails.safe_degrade_manual_approval=true). Note: This does not auto-apply changes; it routes the user into the existing override flow (justification required; RBAC enforced) rather than silently bypassing gating.

Failure modes covered: - Runner hard-down (connection refused / 5xx): circuit breaker opens; policy engine returns SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE within ~200ms. - Runner backlog/timeouts: after timeout threshold (30s) and N consecutive timeouts, circuit breaker opens; subsequent applies are fast-fail with SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE. - Partial outage: if health is DEGRADED but still serving, we continue to attempt gating; only fast-fail when health is UNAVAILABLE or breaker open.

API behavior: - New GatingDecisionStatus: BLOCKED_SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE. - For manual approval tiers, the apply response includes override_allowed=true and override_required=true when safe-degrade triggers; callers must use the existing override endpoint (no change in override permissions). - For blocked tiers, override_allowed remains false.

Small illustrative snippet (Optimize apply handler): if (gatingSystemUnavailable) { const action = safeDegradePolicy.actionForTenant(ctx.tenant); return res.status(200).json({ status: action === 'BLOCK' ? 'BLOCKED_SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE' : 'MANUAL_APPROVAL_REQUIRED', failure_reason: 'SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE', retry_after_seconds: 60, gating_run_id: null }); }

Testing: - Added integration tests that simulate (a) runner down, (b) runner timeout, (c) breaker half-open recovery, and assert deterministic status per tier. - Added unit tests for SafeDegradePolicy mapping and for ensuring we do not emit PII in audit payloads.

Rollout: Guarded by feature flag optimize.guardrails.safe_degrade_enabled. Default off. In observe-only mode we still log the would-have-been safe-degrade outcome in audit event metadata (no behavior change). Next stage is soft enforcement for internal canary, then pilot tenants.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Console wording for the blocked/manual-approval state (Kenji is tracking copy updates). - SRE to tune the circuit breaker thresholds once we have more production data on runner latency distribution.

Links: Linear ENG-3913 (enforcement), ENG-3914 (runner), ENG-3926 (rollout stages), ENG-3919 (monitoring).
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): We should fail closed for all tiers if the runner is down; allowing enterprise to proceed feels risky. Also, please ensure this is fast-fail and does not add tail latency to apply.

Ethan Park (author): Agree on fail-closed by default; for enterprise we are not bypassing evals, only allowing the existing manual approval path (RBAC + justification + audit). Added explicit MANUAL_APPROVAL_REQUIRED status and ensured we short-circuit to <200ms when breaker is open / health UNAVAILABLE.

Jordan Lee: Circuit breaker policy: opening after 3 consecutive failures feels low; can we make it configurable? Also ensure deterministic ordering in the gating response fields (we had flake issues before).

Ethan Park (author): Added config knobs: guardrails.eval_runner.cb_open_after, cb_reset_seconds, and a stable field ordering in the JSON serializer for gating responses. Also added a unit test that snapshots the response payload.

Naomi Feldman (Security): Manual approval path must never be available to non-enterprise tiers and must not expose internal health details to customers. Audit events are fine but please normalize reasons (no raw errors).

Ethan Park (author): Restricted REQUIRE_MANUAL_APPROVAL to tier=ENTERPRISE only; response includes only failure_reason=SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE and retry_after_seconds (no raw errors). Audit event stores normalized unavailable_reason enum + breaker state; raw error remains internal-only in logs with redaction.
Benji Okafor: Migration adds new columns; can we make them nullable with defaults? Also, any impact on existing audit exporters?
Ethan Park (author): Columns are nullable + default 'UNKNOWN'. Export schema version bumped; existing exporters tolerate new fields (verified in staging with SIEM sink).
Chloe Martin: API returning 200 for blocked feels odd; why not 409? Console expects 200 today, but want to confirm we’re consistent.

Ethan Park (author): Kept 200 for backward compatibility with existing apply flow (which treats gating as a business decision, not an error). Added status field to differentiate quality fail vs system unavailable. We can revisit status codes when we rev the apply API.
